references.text: Refers to the seven days of Unleavened Bread that form the context for the holy assemblies mentioned in verse 16.
Repeats the commandment regarding a holy assembly on the first and seventh days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, with a prohibition against work.
Describes the offerings to be brought on the holy assembly days during the Feast of Unleavened Bread, along with the ban on work.
Refers to the seventh day as a sacred assembly for the Lord, where no work is to be done.
The Sabbath commandment that establishes the principle of holy days without work.
Defines the term 'holy assembly' (מִקְרָא־קֹדֶשׁ) in connection with the Sabbath.
Permits food preparation before the Sabbath, serving as background for the exception regarding food preparation in verse 16.
Mentions the day of preparation before a high Sabbath, showing that these holy days were still observed in Jesus' time.
Confirms that the seventh day of Passover has the same status as the first, with a prohibition against work.
Links the ban on work on the seventh day to the duration of offerings throughout the entire festival period.
Establishes the symmetry in the festival law by confirming that the first day carries the same requirement for a holy assembly as the seventh.
Confirms the requirement for a holy assembly and rest on the first day of Passover from another legal text perspective.
